reason: Each FR-06 rule maps to an assertion that fails when it is violated. (1) No Session in the business layer: test_fr06.py:187 AST-scans service/ for the name Session, and :185 checks UnitOfWork is not a Session. (2) Commit on success and rollback on exception: :208/:210 on success, :226/:228/:230 on RuntimeError, :251/:253/:255 on CancelledError, all counting real Session after_commit and after_rollback events and checking persistence. (3) No string-built SQL: :320 AST-scans every module under taskq_api for f-string, % and + SQL. (4) N+1: :383 requires equal statement counts for 10 and 100 seeded rows, and :389 caps the repository count at 2. (5) Pool: :404 and :406 check pool size and pre_ping, but 5 is also the default, so :404 alone would not catch an implementation that ignores TASKQ_DB_POOL_SIZE. The non-default case at :414 (pool_size=7) does catch that.

gaps.message: The declared test test_fr06_engine_pool_size_and_pre_ping uses pool size 5, which equals the default, so its pool-size assertion cannot detect an implementation that ignores TASKQ_DB_POOL_SIZE. Only the undeclared test at line 414 (value 7) does.
The first bullet says all data access goes through repository/. No test checks this beyond the service layer, for example that api/ code does not issue SQL directly.
